subtype: Approach: considering family rules and school norms [Thinking]
passage: The sign-up sheet for the Saturday museum trip closed on Wednesday evening, so Yogesh had one night to decide how to ask Preeti. In the flat he thought it through. His parents liked him home before dark and wanted to know where he was going. The school expected students on trips to stay in groups. A film for two was out. More than that, he did not want Preeti to feel cornered. So: the museum trip, daytime, six or seven classmates, and he would tell Mummy that Preeti was in the group. Next morning at the sign-up table he said, "A few of us are sitting together on the museum trip. Want to join?" Preeti looked at the list and picked up the pen. "Put me next to Anita."

qa.q: When did the sign-up sheet for the museum trip close?
qa.a: The sign-up sheet closed on Wednesday evening.

qa.q: What might Yogesh be worried about while thinking it through?
qa.a: Yogesh is worried about his parents' wishes, the school's group rule, safety, and not making Preeti feel cornered.

qa.q: What alternative setting could Yogesh use if there were no museum trip, and why?
qa.a: Yogesh could invite Preeti to a daytime group project at the library, because a group in daylight keeps things safe and comfortable for both.

qa.q: How might Yogesh's parents see the plan?
qa.a: They would likely feel reassured, since it is a daytime group outing and Yogesh is honest about who will be there.

grounding: The student thinks about family expectations and school rules and chooses a daytime group setting, with safety, honesty with parents and comfort for both people in mind.
